passage:
My name is Lalremsiami, and people sometimes ask me how you know when to raise something at work. For me it wasn't one big thing. It was small things repeating.
Every month-end, the same three supplier accounts got "adjustments" late at night, always from my boss's login. Bhupen said it was rounding. It happened eleven months in a row.
Then the auditors came, and he asked me to "not bother them with the supplier folder". When I said the auditors might want it, he laughed a bit too loudly.
I didn't know what it meant. Maybe nothing. But I couldn't keep carrying the doubt.
So I didn't accuse anyone. I used the company's ethics line and wrote down only what I had seen: dates, accounts, what he said.
The ethics officer called me that same afternoon. She thanked me, said it would be reviewed independently, and that no one was allowed to punish me for raising it.

qa.q: How many months in a row did the adjustments happen?
qa.a: The adjustments happened eleven months in a row.

qa.q: What was Lalremsiami feeling before using the ethics line?
qa.a: Lalremsiami felt a heavy doubt that would not go away, unsure whether it meant anything but unable to keep carrying it silently.

qa.q: Why was using the ethics line with only facts a sound choice?
qa.a: It raised the concern early through the proper channel, stuck to dates, accounts and Bhupen's words, and avoided accusing anyone of something unproven.

qa.q: How did the ethics officer respond to the report?
qa.a: The ethics officer called the same afternoon, thanked Lalremsiami, promised an independent review and said no one was allowed to punish Lalremsiami for raising it.

grounding: Lalremsiami notices repeated odd adjustments and a boss resisting the auditors, and raises the doubt early through the proper ethics channel.

passage:
I've worked two desks down from Chandrika at the cooperative bank for three years, so I'll only tell you what I actually saw.
Last year she started wearing new gold every few weeks and talked about a flat in the new tower. Her salary is the same as mine. That alone meant nothing; families help, people inherit.
But I'm the one who reconciles the dormant accounts. Twice in spring, small amounts moved out of two old accounts on days Chandrika was on the counter. Both times the reversal slip was missing.
I don't know what was in her mind. I don't know if she did anything at all.
I sat with it for a week, feeling sick. Then I wrote down the dates and account numbers, nothing else, for the internal auditor.
The auditor read it in front of me. "You were right to bring this now, Devika. We'll check quietly. Your name stays with me."

qa.q: What was missing both times money moved out of the old accounts?
qa.a: Both times the reversal slip was missing.

qa.q: How did Devika feel during the week before going to the auditor?
qa.a: Devika felt sick and torn, unsure whether Chandrika had done anything and uneasy about carrying the doubt alone.

qa.q: What made Devika's way of raising the concern fair?
qa.a: Devika reported early, gave only dates and account numbers to the internal auditor, and did not accuse Chandrika of anything unproven.

qa.q: How did the internal auditor respond?
qa.a: The auditor read the note in front of Devika, said bringing it now was right, promised to check quietly, and kept Devika's name private.

grounding: Devika notices Chandrika living beyond her means alongside odd account movements and raises the doubt early and factually with the internal auditor.

passage:
First week, a Tuesday: Uma noticed a small "rounding adjustment" in the vendor ledger, signed off by her manager, Karthik. Odd, but small. She let it go.
Third week, a Thursday: there were four more, all to the same vendor, each just under the amount that needed a second signature. When the internal audit team asked to review the ledger, Karthik told them the team was "too busy this month" and to come back next quarter. Uma's stomach knotted. Maybe she was imagining it. Maybe she'd lose her job for asking.
Fifth week, a Monday: Uma wrote down dates, entry numbers and amounts, without accusing anyone, and sent them through the company's ethics line, which the handbook said was confidential. Then she went back to her desk and tried to breathe normally.
Two days later, the auditors arrived anyway.

qa.q: What did Karthik tell the internal audit team?
qa.a: That the team was 'too busy this month' and to come back next quarter.

qa.q: What was Uma feeling in the third week?
qa.a: Uma's stomach knotted; Uma felt anxious and unsure, wondering if it was imagination and afraid of losing the job for asking.

qa.q: Which step did Uma take, and why is it a good channel?
qa.a: Uma recorded dates, entry numbers and amounts without accusing anyone and sent them through the confidential ethics line, so the right people could check.

qa.q: How might Karthik see the auditors arriving anyway?
qa.a: Karthik, who had tried to delay the review, would likely feel exposed and alarmed that the adjustments would now be examined.

grounding: Shows an employee noticing repeated odd adjustments and a manager resisting audit, and raising it early through the proper channel.

passage:
Lalremsiami, you asked why I always say "raise it early". Let me tell you about Prakash.
Twenty years ago, Prakash and I sat side by side in the purchase department in Guwahati. Same salary, same bus. Then one year he bought a car. Then a flat. His wife wore new gold every festival. He laughed and said, "Chetan, relax, my father-in-law is generous."
I noticed other things too. He always stayed late when the invoices were being cleared. He never took leave, not even for his daughter's school function. I told myself it was none of my business.
Two years later the auditors found a fake supplier. Prakash lost his job and nearly went to jail. Three honest clerks were suspended for months while it was sorted out, and one of them was me.
If I had gone to the vigilance officer in that first year, with just what I had seen, it would have been smaller. For him too.

qa.q: What did Prakash buy first?
qa.a: He bought a car.

qa.q: How did young Chetan feel about what was noticed back then?
qa.a: Young Chetan felt uneasy but pushed the doubt away, deciding it was none of Chetan's business.

qa.q: What choice inside the story could have made things smaller?
qa.a: Going to the vigilance officer in the first year with just what was seen, instead of staying silent for two years.

qa.q: How might Prakash's fall have looked to his family?
qa.a: His family, who had seen the new gold and the flat, would have faced shock and shame when he lost his job and nearly went to jail.

grounding: Shows an elder recalling a colleague living beyond his means and resisting leave, and how raising the doubt early would have limited the harm.

passage:
Leela had been at the animal shelter trust for four months, still on probation, when she noticed it. The donation-box totals in the register never matched the deposit slips. Always a little lower. Maria, the finance officer, kept the slips in her own drawer and said, "Don't worry about accounts, you do the adoptions."
Then the auditor's visit, planned for Friday, was suddenly postponed. Maria had called and said the files were "being reorganised".
Leela had no proof, only a pattern. The director was abroad. The power kept cutting out, and the office smelled of wet dogs and kerosene.
That evening, by the light of her phone, she wrote a short, plain email to the trust's board treasurer: the dates, the two sets of numbers, the postponed audit. No accusations. "I may be wrong. I'd rather ask early."
She hovered over send, thinking of her probation. Then she pressed it.

qa.q: Where did Maria keep the deposit slips?
qa.a: Maria kept the slips in her own drawer.

qa.q: What was Leela feeling as she hovered over send?
qa.a: Leela felt anxious about probation and unsure without proof, yet chose to raise the pattern early.

qa.q: Why was Leela's email a good way to raise the concern?
qa.a: It went to the board treasurer, a proper channel, with dates and numbers and no accusations, admitting Leela might be wrong.

qa.q: How might Maria react when the board treasurer starts asking questions?
qa.a: Maria, who postponed the audit and kept the slips, would likely feel cornered and anxious, whether or not there is an innocent explanation.

grounding: Shows a new employee noticing mismatched totals and a postponed audit, and raising the doubt early and calmly through the board.

passage: On the fourteenth floor of the Salt Lake office, Zeenat noticed it again at month-end: a round "adjustment" in the vendor account, approved by Mr Sen, with no invoice attached. It was the fourth month in a row. When internal audit emailed to schedule a visit, Mr Sen postponed it, twice, saying the team was too busy. Zeenat mentioned it to Trisha over lunch. Trisha shrugged. "He's the boss. And he just bought a new car. Maybe business is good. Don't get involved." Zeenat pushed rice around her plate. Maybe there was an innocent reason. She didn't want to accuse anyone. But four blank entries and two postponed audits weren't nothing. That evening she wrote down dates and amounts, only what she had seen, no guesses about motives. On Thursday she used the company's confidential ethics line, as the handbook said, and asked compliance to look. She felt sick sending it, and then, strangely, lighter.

qa.q: How many times did Mr Sen postpone the audit?
qa.a: Twice.

qa.q: How did Zeenat feel about raising the issue?
qa.a: Zeenat felt uneasy and torn, not wanting to accuse anyone, then sick while sending the report and afterwards lighter.

qa.q: What made Zeenat's report careful and fair?
qa.a: She recorded only the dates and amounts she had seen, made no guesses about motives, and used the confidential ethics line as the handbook said.

qa.q: Why might Trisha prefer not to get involved?
qa.a: Trisha may feel uneasy about crossing the boss and want to avoid trouble, so she reaches for an innocent explanation.

grounding: Shows a team member noticing repeated odd adjustments and a boss who delays audits, and raising the doubt early through the proper channel.
